evidence: DETERMINISM OF PINNED VALUES - holds on source inspection. (1) Static baseline, nothing regenerated or fetched: solution/solve.sh is `cp -a "$(dirname "$0")/app/." /app/` plus an rm of the disposable DB files under /app; no npm install, curl, git or code generation. package.json pins express 5.1.0 and better-sqlite3 12.4.1, the same versions the agent Dockerfile installs globally. A grep of solution/ for fetch(/http(s):// finds only the browser's same-origin `fetch(path, ...)` in public/js/app.js:40; index.html and styles.css reference no remote URL. (2) Seeding is a pure function of the co-located roster: src/db.js:122-180 seedIfEmpty returns when users is non-empty (line 124), otherwise inserts in one transaction, iterating roster arrays in file order; every seeded id is either the roster id or a deterministic composite (`GR-${offer_id}` :162, `RM-${offer_id}-${kind}` :167, `RA-${offer_id}` :172); every seeded created_at is REF = roster reference_moment (:127). The AUTOINCREMENT tables (commitment_movements, after_images, audit_log) get ids from insertion order, which is fixed. solution/app/src/seed_data.json and environment/assets/seed_data.json are byte-identical (sha256 1b39015461a7a4f2...), so the fallback chain at db.js:14 cannot move a figure. (3) No wall clock in graded rules: `const now = () => R.refAt(db)` (src/index.js:62) reads system_clock, seeded from reference_moment "2026-08-01T00:00:00Z" (seed_data.json:3); every created_at/approved_at/rescinded_at write goes through now(). No Date.now(), argument-less new Date(), performance.now or CURRENT_TIMESTAMP exists anywhere in solution/; every `new Date(...)` in src/rules.js (lines 29-42) takes a stored or supplied ISO string and uses UTC accessors only. Signing/equity clawback uses the rescission's own effective date (index.js:411-413), referral vesting uses now() (index.js:194). (4) Arithmetic is integer/BigInt with one half-up rounding (rules.js:54-55); no float accumulation. (5) Read ordering is explicit: every multi-row read in index.js:150-240 and change-sets.js:93 carries ORDER BY id/rowid; in-memory sorts use plain code-unit comparison (change-sets.js:57, :80), no localeCompare. Money formatting uses toLocaleString('en-US') with an explicit locale; client fmtTime (public/js/app.js:63) pins timeZone 'UTC'. (6) Randomness exists but lands on no pinned value: session token crypto.randomBytes(24) (index.js:112); change-set id uid('CS') (change-sets.js:109); revised-offer id is deterministic `${o.id}-R` with a random uid('OFF') only on collision (index.js:381-382, change-sets.js:132-133); the client pre-fills random suggestions for requisition/offer ids and operation keys (public/js/hireops.js:39,65,208; public/js/change-sets.js:18,44,169). The rubric explicitly does not pin these: functional/judge.toml:497 'Do not require a specific generated-ID format', :929 'Discover generated IDs from results', functional/prompt.md:17 and :27 'IDs may be generated; read them from results'. A grep of all judge.toml/prompt/app_context files for a literal '-R' offer id or 'CS-<hex>' id found none. HASH BINDING: all 14 frozen solution files hash to the values in raw-evidence-index.json matching_source_files (e.g. src/index.js b0303a5c..., solve.sh 1df2ed04...), and are byte-identical to the current working tree. WHAT DOES NOT HOLD - the 'committed' half of the row: 6 of the 14 frozen solution files differ from git HEAD (5b1df041) and show as ' M' in git status: public/js/app.js (HEAD 7b03d407... vs frozen 5c4e3011...), public/js/change-sets.js, public/js/hireops.js, public/styles.css, src/change-sets.js, src/index.js. The candidate under review is therefore a hash-frozen snapshot but not a committed baseline. NOT MEASURED: I did not run the app. better-sqlite3 is not installed on the host and this assignment starts no container, so 'seed twice into fresh DBs and diff the dumps' was not executed; the determinism conclusion rests on reading the code. The scripted golden runs in the evidence index do not test repeat-seed equality and I did not use them as proof of it.
counterexample: No graded figure was found that can move between runs. Probes tried: (a) broken-but-passing: a reference that stamped created_at from Date.now() would still pass any criterion that only reads derived money figures - not the case here, since now() is the stored clock; (b) conforming-but-failing: a second revision of an offer whose '<id>-R' already exists gets a random OFF-XXXXXXXX id, which would fail a criterion pinning the '-R' form - no criterion pins it (judge.toml:497 forbids requiring a format). The only confirmed gap is procedural: checking out HEAD today yields a different reference (6 files) from the one frozen under input sha 52feadde..., so the git history cannot reproduce the reviewed golden.
suggested_fix: Commit the six modified solution files (owner action; reviewers may not write to git) so the frozen bytes equal a commit, then confirm `git status --short` is clean for solution/ before packaging. Optionally have the owner run one double-seed diff (two fresh DB_PATH files, compare `sqlite3 .dump` excluding sessions) in the verifier image to convert the source reading into a measurement.
